description: Soft, layered Kenyan flatbreads made from wheat flour, a beloved accompaniment to stews and tea.

steps.instruction: Mix flour and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide into 6–8 balls, cover and rest for 30 minutes. Roll thin, brush with oil, fold into a spiral and roll again.
Cook on a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden spots appear.

serving_suggestion: Serve with beef stew, beans or tea.

description: Soft, sweet fried dough triangles—a beloved Kenyan teatime snack.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, sugar and salt. Add milk and knead into a soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes.
Roll out and cut into triangles.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown. Drain and serve warm.

description: Sweet, syrupy fried dough balls from the Kenyan coast, often served during Ramadan and celebrations.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, coconut milk and cardamom into a thick batter.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry until golden. Drain.
Boil sugar with a little water to make syrup, toss fried balls in syrup and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a sweet snack with tea.

description: Bright, tangy Kenyan rice made with fresh lemon juice and zest, a simple side that pairs well with stews.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice. Heat oil and sauté chopped onion until soft.
Add rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in water and salt, bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 18–20 minutes.
Squeeze lemon juice over cooked rice and grate in some zest. Fluff gently and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled fish or chicken stew.

description: Chicken pieces cooked with fresh lemon juice, garlic and onions for a bright, tangy Kenyan stew.

steps.instruction: Brown chicken in oil for 6–8 minutes. Remove.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add lemon juice and water.
Return chicken, season with salt and simmer for 20 minutes until cooked. Serve with rice.

description: Fresh, homemade Kenyan lemonade made with lemon juice, sugar and water—refreshing on a hot day.

steps.instruction: Squeeze lemons to extract juice.
Mix lemon juice, sugar and water in a jug. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Chill and serve over ice.

serving_suggestion: Serve chilled as a refreshing drink.

description: A fresh Kenyan salad of tomatoes, red onion and coriander dressed with tangy lime juice.

steps.instruction: Dice tomatoes and red onion. Chop coriander.
Combine in a bowl and squeeze lime juice over.
Add salt, toss gently and serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve with nyama choma or pilau.

description: Chicken pieces marinated with lime juice, garlic and a touch of chilli, then grilled until charred.

steps.instruction: Mix lime juice, crushed garlic, chilli, oil and salt. Coat chicken and marinate for 20 minutes.
Grill over medium heat for 8–10 minutes per side until cooked through and charred.
Serve hot with kachumbari or rice.

description: A refreshing Kenyan drink made with fresh lime juice, sugar and water.

steps.instruction: Squeeze limes to extract juice.
Mix lime juice, sugar and water in a jug. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Chill and serve over ice.

serving_suggestion: Serve chilled as a refreshing drink.

description: Rice cooked with carrots, green beans and onions, a colourful and nutritious Kenyan side dish.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice. Sauté onion in oil until soft. Add chopped carrots and green beans and cook for 3 minutes.
Add rice and stir to coat. Pour in water and salt.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with beef stew or grilled chicken.

description: A creamy Kenyan rice pudding made with milk, sugar and a hint of cardamom.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice and combine with milk in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until rice is soft and creamy.
Stir in sugar and cardamom. Serve warm or chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a dessert or snack.

description: A one-pot Kenyan dish of rice cooked with beans and a tomato-onion base—hearty and economical.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add beans, rice, salt and water.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender. Fluff and serve.

description: Tender beans simmered in a rich tomato and onion sauce, a protein-packed Kenyan staple.

steps.instruction: Soak beans overnight or boil for 5 minutes and let sit for 1 hour. Drain and boil in fresh water for 45–60 minutes until tender.
Sauté onions in oil until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cooked beans and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes. Season and serve with ugali.

description: A comforting Kenyan soup of beans simmered with onions, tomatoes and garlic.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened. Add beans and water.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes, mashing some beans to thicken. Season and serve.

description: A classic Kenyan combination of beans stew served over fluffy rice.

steps.instruction: Cook rice in salted water until tender. Set aside.
Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve beans stew over the rice.

description: Chicken pieces simmered in a savory tomato and onion base—a comforting everyday Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Boil chicken pieces with salt and water until tender, about 25–30 minutes. Reserve broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add boiled chicken and reserved broth. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until flavors meld. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: Chicken pieces cooked in a rich, spiced tomato and onion curry sauce with Indian influences.

steps.instruction: Brown chicken in oil for 6–8 minutes. Remove.
Sauté onions until golden. Add curry powder and tomatoes, cook until thick.
Return chicken, add water and salt, simmer for 20–25 minutes. Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Fragrant spiced rice cooked with chicken pieces, pilau masala and caramelised onions.

steps.instruction: Fry onions until deep golden. Add pilau masala and chicken, brown for 5 minutes.
Add 2 cups water and simmer until chicken is tender, about 20 minutes.
Add rice and remaining water, season with salt. Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes. Serve.

description: A rich, slow-cooked Kenyan beef stew with onions, tomatoes and garlic.

steps.instruction: Brown beef in hot oil. Remove.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Return beef, add water and salt, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until tender.

description: A fragrant Kenyan spiced rice dish cooked with pilau masala, beef and caramelised onions.

steps.instruction: Heat oil and fry onions until deep golden brown.
Add pilau masala and beef, brown. Add 2 cups water and simmer until beef is tender.
Add rice and remaining water, season with salt. Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes. Fluff and serve.

description: Tender beef cubes simmered in a spiced curry sauce with onions and tomatoes.

steps.instruction: Brown beef in oil. Remove.
Sauté onions until golden. Add curry powder and tomatoes, cook until thick.
Return beef, add water and salt, simmer for 40 minutes until tender. Serve with rice.

description: Extra-sweet Kenyan mandazi with a higher sugar content, a favourite teatime treat.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, sugar and salt. Add milk and knead into a soft dough.
Rest for 15 minutes, roll out and cut into triangles.
Fry in hot oil until golden. Drain and serve.

description: Crunchy peanuts coated in caramelised sugar, a popular Kenyan snack.

steps.instruction: Roast groundnuts lightly and set aside.
Melt sugar with water in a pan until caramel forms.
Stir in peanuts, coat well, spread on a tray and cool before breaking into pieces.

description: A sweet Kenyan millet porridge, sweetened with sugar and often served for breakfast.

steps.instruction: Mix millet flour with 1 cup water to make a paste.
Bring remaining water to a boil, stir in paste and cook for 10 minutes.
Add sugar, stir and serve warm.

description: Chicken pieces cooked in a vibrant green coriander sauce with yogurt and spices.

steps.instruction: Blend coriander, yogurt and garlic into a green paste.
Brown chicken in oil. Remove. Sauté onion until soft.
Return chicken, stir in coriander paste and salt, simmer for 20 minutes. Serve with rice.

description: Fragrant rice cooked with fresh coriander paste and onions, a green and flavourful Kenyan side.

steps.instruction: Blend coriander with a little water into a paste.
Sauté onion in oil until soft. Add coriander paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add rice, water and salt. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled chicken or fish.

description: A fresh, tangy Kenyan chutney made from coriander, green chilli, lemon and garlic.

steps.instruction: Wash coriander and chop roughly. Deseed chilli.
Blend coriander, chilli, lemon juice, garlic and salt into a smooth paste.
Serve as a condiment with grilled meats or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with nyama choma or samosas.

description: Fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk—a coastal Kenyan favourite often served with fish or stew.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice. Heat oil and sauté onion until soft.
Add rice and stir. Pour in coconut milk, water and salt.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with fish curry or bean stew.

description: Tilapia simmered in a rich coconut milk curry with onions, tomatoes, garlic and ginger.

steps.instruction: Clean and score tilapia, rub with salt.
Sauté onion, garlic and ginger. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Pour in coconut milk.
Add fish, cover and simmer for 10–12 minutes until cooked and sauce thickens.

serving_suggestion: Serve with coconut rice or chapati.

description: Beans simmered in a creamy coconut milk sauce with onions, tomatoes and garlic.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add beans and coconut milk.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes until thick. Season and serve with rice.
